chunks: From him, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ali ibn Isma'il, from Isma'il ibn 'Ammar and others, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I said to him, 'I take the dirhams from a man, weigh them, and then distribute them, so some remain in my hand.' He said, 'Do you not strive for accuracy/completeness?' I said, 'Yes.' He said, 'There is no harm.'
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to keep leftover coins after weighing them for distribution?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) validates the practice of retaining a small surplus of coins after weighing and distributing them, provided the merchant strives for exactness (*wafa'*). This ruling highlights the Shia juristic emphasis on intent and precision in commercial transactions, distinguishing permissible minor discrepancies from deceitful short-changing. It serves as a foundational text for understanding the flexibility within strict Islamic trade ethics regarding currency exchange.
